key_insight: First-principles calculations identify a class of 109° domain walls in rhombohedral R3c NaNbO₃ with a notably low energy of 9 mJ m⁻².
engineering_relevance: The findings could inform domain and phase-transition engineering in ferroelectric oxides, but the abstract reports neither AI methods nor solar-cell applications.
method: Classify eight unique domain-wall classes using group theory.
Apply elastic compatibility and charge neutrality constraints.
Perform first-principles structural relaxations for representative walls.
evidence_signal: The calculated low-energy 109° wall class is compatible with experimentally observed crystal twinning and motivates a proposed atomistic R3c ↔ Pbcm transition mechanism.
watch_item: The proposed transition mechanism requires validation; the abstract reports no device-level performance evaluation.
